license_required.quote: It is unlawful for any person to practice medicine, osteopathic medicine, chiropractic, or podiatry or as a physician assistant in the Commonwealth without a valid unrevoked license issued by the Board.

type.quote: The Board of Medicine shall consist of one medical physician from each congressional district, one osteopathic physician, one podiatrist, one chiropractor, and four citizen members.

umbrella_agency.quote: The following boards are included within the Department: Board of Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology, Board of Counseling, Board of Dentistry, Board of Funeral Directors and Embalmers, Board of Long-Term Care Administrators, Board of Medicine, Board of Nursing, Board of Optometry, Board of Pharmacy, Board of Physical Therapy, Board of Psychology, Board of Social Work, and Board of Veterinary Medicine.

exams.notes: Also accepted: Federation of State Medical Boards, National Board of Osteopathic Medical Examiners, or other examinations as determined by the Board. Minimum passing score determined by the Board.
exams.quote: The examinations of candidates for licensure to practice medicine and osteopathy shall be those of the National Board of Medical Examiners, the Federation of State Medical Boards, the National Board of Osteopathic Medical Examiners, or such other examinations as determined by the Board.

interval_years.quote: Every license granted under the provisions of this chapter shall be renewed biennially as prescribed by the Board.

required.quote: The Board shall prescribe by regulation such requirements as may be necessary to ensure continued practitioner competence, which may include continuing education, testing, or any other requirement.

value: up to two hours of Type 1 continuing learning activities or courses in a specific subject area as designated by the Board
topical_requirements.quote: any licensee of the Board of Medicine may be required by the Board to complete up to two hours of Type 1 continuing learning activities or courses in a specific subject area.

available.quote: The Board, in its discretion, may issue certificates or licenses to applicants upon endorsement by boards or other appropriate authorities of other states or territories or the District of Columbia with which reciprocal relations have not been established if the credentials of such applicants are satisfactory and the examinations and passing grades required by such other boards are fully equal to those required by the Virginia Board.

requirements.value: The Board may issue licenses by endorsement if credentials are satisfactory and examinations/passing grades of the other board are fully equal to Virginia's. The Board shall prioritize applicants from contiguous states through a streamlined process with a final determination within 20 days of a completed application.
requirements.quote: The Board of Medicine shall prioritize applicants for licensure as a doctor of medicine or osteopathic medicine, a physician assistant, or an advanced practice registered nurse from such states that are contiguous with the Commonwealth in processing their applications for licensure by endorsement through a streamlined process, with a final determination regarding qualification to be made within 20 days of the receipt of a completed application.

disciplinary_grounds.description: False statements, representations, fraud, or deceit in obtaining admission to practice or in practice of any branch of healing arts
disciplinary_grounds.quote: False statements or representations or fraud or deceit in obtaining admission to the practice, or fraud or deceit in the practice of any branch of the healing arts;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Substance abuse rendering the practitioner unfit for performance of professional obligations and duties
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Substance abuse rendering him unfit for the performance of his professional obligations and duties;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Intentional or negligent conduct in the practice of any branch of healing arts that causes or is likely to cause injury to a patient
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Intentional or negligent conduct in the practice of any branch of the healing arts that causes or is likely to cause injury to a patient or patients;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Mental or physical incapacity or incompetence to practice the profession with safety to patients and the public
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Mental or physical incapacity or incompetence to practice his profession with safety to his patients and the public;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Restriction of a license to practice a branch of healing arts in another state, D.C., U.S. possession or territory, foreign jurisdiction, or federal entity
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Restriction of a license to practice a branch of the healing arts in another state, the District of Columbia, a United States possession or territory, or a foreign jurisdiction, or for an entity of the federal government;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Procuring, performing, or aiding a criminal abortion
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Undertaking in any manner or by any means whatsoever to procure or perform or aid or abet in procuring or performing a criminal abortion;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing under a false or assumed name or impersonating another practitioner
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Engaging in the practice of any of the healing arts under a false or assumed name, or impersonating another practitioner of a like, similar, or different name;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Prescribing or dispensing controlled substances with intent they will be used other than medicinally or to evade law
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Prescribing or dispensing any controlled substance with intent or knowledge that it will be used otherwise than medicinally, or for accepted therapeutic purposes, or with intent to evade any law with respect to the sale, use, or disposition of such drug;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating provisions on division of fees or practicing in violation of chapter provisions
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violating provisions of this chapter on division of fees or practicing any branch of the healing arts in violation of the provisions of this chapter;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Knowingly and willfully committing a felony under Commonwealth or federal law, or a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Knowingly and willfully committing an act that is a felony under the laws of the Commonwealth or the United States, or any act that is a misdemeanor under such laws and involves moral turpitude;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Aiding, abetting, having professional connection with, or lending name to person known to be illegally practicing healing arts
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Aiding or abetting, having professional connection with, or lending his name to any person known to him to be practicing illegally any of the healing arts;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conducting practice contrary to the standards of ethics of the branch of healing arts
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conducting his practice in a manner contrary to the standards of ethics of his branch of the healing arts;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conducting practice in a manner that is a danger to health and welfare of patients or the public
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conducting his practice in such a manner as to be a danger to the health and welfare of his patients or to the public;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Inability to practice with reasonable skill or safety because of illness or substance abuse
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Inability to practice with reasonable skill or safety because of illness or substance abuse;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Publishing an advertisement that claims superiority or violates Board advertising regulations
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Publishing in any manner an advertisement relating to his professional practice that contains a claim of superiority or violates Board regulations governing advertising;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Performing any act likely to deceive, defraud, or harm the public
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Performing any act likely to deceive, defraud, or harm the public;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating any provision of statute or regulation relating to manufacture, distribution, dispensing, or administration of drugs
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violating any provision of statute or regulation, state or federal, relating to the manufacture, distribution, dispensing, or administration of drugs;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating or cooperating with others in violating any provisions of applicable chapters or Board regulations
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violating or cooperating with others in violating any of the provisions of Chapters 1 (§ 54.1-100 et seq.), 24 (§ 54.1-2400 et seq.) and this chapter or regulations of the Board;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in sexual contact with a patient concurrent with the practitioner-patient relationship or engaging in lewd conduct toward a patient
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Engaging in sexual contact with a patient concurrent with and by virtue of the practitioner and patient relationship or otherwise engaging at any time during the course of the practitioner and patient relationship in conduct of a sexual nature that a reasonable patient would consider lewd and offensive;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction in any state, territory, or country of a felony or crime involving moral turpitude
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction in any state, territory, or country of any felony or of any crime involving moral turpitude;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Adjudication of legal incompetence or incapacity in any state if currently in effect
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Adjudication of legal incompetence or incapacity in any state if such adjudication is in effect and the person has not been declared restored to competence or capacity;

disciplinary_grounds.description: Performing medical examiner services while not listed on the National Registry of Certified Medical Examiners or failing to meet continuing requirements
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Performing the services of a medical examiner as defined in 49 C.F.R. § 390.5 if, at the time such services are performed, the person performing such services is not listed on the National Registry of Certified Medical Examiners

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing or refusing to complete and file electronically the medical certification using the Electronic Death Registration System
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing or refusing to complete and file electronically using the Electronic Death Registration System any medical certification in accordance with the requirements of subsection C of § 32.1-263.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in a pattern of violations of § 38.2-3445.01
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Engaging in a pattern of violations of § 38.2-3445.01.

definition_quote.value: "Practice of medicine or osteopathic medicine" means the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of human physical or mental ailments, conditions, diseases, pain, or infirmities by any means or method.
definition_quote.quote: "Practice of medicine or osteopathic medicine" means the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of human physical or mental ailments, conditions, diseases, pain, or infirmities by any means or method.

value: treatment by any means or method
methods_authorized.quote: the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of human physical or mental ailments, conditions, diseases, pain, or infirmities by any means or method.

drug_authority.value: Physicians licensed to practice medicine or osteopathy may administer, prescribe, and dispense controlled substances to patients in a bona fide medical emergency or when pharmaceutical services are not available; also may prescribe dosages of pain-relieving agents in excess of recommended dosages upon certifying medical necessity.
drug_authority.quote: this prohibition shall not apply to a doctor of medicine, osteopathy or podiatry who administers controlled substances to his patients or provides controlled substances to his patient in a bona fide medical emergency or when pharmaceutical services are not available.

license_status_types.quote: The Board may issue a retiree license to any doctor of medicine, osteopathy, podiatry, or chiropractic who holds an unrestricted, active license to practice in the Commonwealth

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Foreign graduates must exhibit a diploma, license, or certificate conferring full right to practice in their country or satisfactory evidence of equivalent study and examinations. The Board may issue a nonrenewable temporary license (up to 2 years) for advanced training in an approved institute, or a provisional license (up to 2 years) to foreign graduates with at least 5 years of practice, ECFMG certification, passing scores on USMLE Steps 1 and 2 CK, and an agreement with a medical care facility for an assessment program.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: Every candidate who is a graduate of a school of a country other than the United States and Canada must, in addition to meeting the other requirements of this article, exhibit to the Board a diploma, license or certificate conferring the full right to practice in that country, or satisfactory evidence showing that the candidate has completed the course of study and passed examinations equivalent to those required for a diploma or license conferring such full right to practice.

postgraduate_training_years_required.quote: Has completed at least 12 months of satisfactory postgraduate training in one program or institution approved by an accrediting agency recognized by the Board for internships or residency training.

pain_management_education_required.quote: The Board shall adopt regulations for the prescribing of opioids and products containing buprenorphine.

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: The Board shall adopt regulations for prescribing opioids including requirements for patient history and evaluation, limitations on dosages or day supply of drugs for acute pain, documentation requirements, and mandatory use of the Prescription Monitoring Program. Chronic pain treatment must include a treatment plan, signed patient agreement, and periodic review.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: The Board shall adopt regulations for the prescribing of opioids and products containing buprenorphine. Such regulations shall include guidelines for: 1. The treatment of acute pain, which shall include (i) requirements for an appropriate patient history and evaluation, (ii) limitations on dosages or day supply of drugs prescribed

controlled_substance_database_registrati.quote: a requirement that the prescriber request and review information contained in the Prescription Monitoring Program in accordance with § 54.1-2522.1

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: An out-of-state doctor of medicine or osteopathy who holds an active, unrestricted license in another state and has a previously established practitioner-patient relationship (with in-person examination within previous 12 months) may provide continuity of care via telemedicine services in the Commonwealth for up to one year per patient for behavioral health services, or for other care generally under an exemption from licensure.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: any doctor of medicine or osteopathy, physician assistant, respiratory therapist, occupational therapist, or advanced practice registered nurse who would otherwise be subject to licensure by the Board who holds an active, unrestricted license in another state or the District of Columbia and who is in good standing with the applicable regulatory agency in that state or the District of Columbia from engaging in the practice of that profession in the Commonwealth with a patient located in the Commonwealth when (i) such practice is for the purpose of providing continuity of care through the use of telemedicine services as defined in § 38.2-3418.16 and (ii) the patient is a current patient of the practitioner with whom the practitioner has previously established a practitioner-patient relationship and the practitioner has performed an in-person examination of the patient within the previous 12 months.

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: every physician assistant shall practice as part of a patient care team and shall provide care in accordance with a written or electronic practice agreement with one or more patient care team physicians or patient care team podiatrists.

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: A licensed physician assistant has authority to prescribe controlled substances and devices as set forth in Chapter 34 as provided in a practice agreement or by credentialing and privileging requirements. Practice agreements must include a statement of controlled substances the PA is or is not authorized to prescribe.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: a licensed physician assistant shall have the authority to prescribe controlled substances and devices as set forth in Chapter 34 (§ 54.1-3400 et seq.) and as provided in a practice agreement or by the credentialing and privileging practice arrangement requirements of a facility

max_physician_assistants_per_supervising.quote: No patient care team physician or patient care team podiatrist shall be allowed to collaborate or consult with more than six physician assistants on a patient care team at any one time.

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: Any malpractice judgment against a person licensed under this chapter; Any settlement of a malpractice claim against a person licensed under this chapter

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: Any disciplinary action taken during or at the conclusion of disciplinary proceedings or while under investigation, including but not limited to denial or termination of employment, denial or termination of privileges or restriction of privileges that results from conduct involving (i) intentional or negligent conduct that causes or is likely to cause injury to a patient or patients

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: When a board has probable cause to believe a practitioner is unable to practice with reasonable skill and safety to patients because of excessive use of alcohol or drugs or physical or mental illness, the board, after preliminary investigation by an informal fact-finding proceeding, may direct that the practitioner submit to a mental or physical examination.

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: When a board has probable cause to believe a practitioner is unable to practice with reasonable skill and safety to patients because of excessive use of alcohol or drugs or physical or mental illness, the board, after preliminary investigation by an informal fact-finding proceeding, may direct that the practitioner submit to a mental or physical examination. Failure to submit to the examination shall constitute grounds for disciplinary action.

scope__license_status_types.quote: To issue inactive licenses or certificates and promulgate regulations to carry out such purpose.
The Board may issue a retiree license to any doctor of medicine, osteopathy, podiatry, or chiropractic who holds an unrestricted, active license to practice in the Commonwealth

The Board may issue authorization to practice valid for a period not to exceed three months to a practitioner of the healing arts licensed or certified and in good standing with the applicable regulatory agency in the state, District of Columbia, or Canada where the practitioner resides when the practitioner is in Virginia temporarily
The Board may issue a restricted volunteer license to a practitioner of the healing arts who: 1. Held an unrestricted license issued by the Virginia Board of Medicine or by a board in another state
place any person on probation for such time as it may designate
suspend any license for a stated period of time or indefinitely
revoke any license for any of the following acts of unprofessional conduct

To take appropriate disciplinary action for violations of applicable law and regulations and to accept, in their discretion, the surrender of a license, certificate, registration, permit, or multistate licensure privilege in lieu of disciplinary action.

the Board may issue a limited license to practice medicine in the hospitals and outpatient clinics of the school or college or in a hospital formally affiliated with the medical school for purposes of undergraduate or postgraduate medical education to a graduate of a foreign medical school as long as he serves as a full-time or adjunct faculty member.

The Board may issue a restricted volunteer license to a practitioner of the healing arts who: 1. Held an unrestricted license issued by the Virginia Board of Medicine or by a board in another state as a licensee in good standing at the time the license expired or became inactive; 2. Is practicing within the limits of his license in accordance with provisions of § 54.1-106

The Board of Medicine shall prioritize applicants for licensure as a doctor of medicine or osteopathic medicine, a physician assistant, or an advanced practice registered nurse from such states that are contiguous with the Commonwealth in processing their applications for licensure by endorsement through a streamlined process, with a final determination regarding qualification to be made within 20 days of the receipt of a completed application.

Upon recommendation by the chief of an approved internship or residency program as defined in this chapter, the Board may issue a temporary annual license to practice medicine, osteopathic medicine, or podiatry to interns and residents in such programs.
